name: Kaldera Vast
geological_features: Deep canyon networks carved by ancient water
Massive impact craters filled with crystallized sand
specific_features: Glass plains formed by prehistoric meteor bombardment
Subsurface salt caverns of immense scale
description: Kaldera Vast is an enormous desert world dominated by continent-sized dune fields and yawning canyon systems that plunge dozens of kilometers into the crust. Its sheer scale dwarfs most terrestrial planets, with horizons that seem to stretch into infinity beneath a pale amber sky.

The thin atmosphere offers little protection from solar radiation, and the temperature swings between bone-cracking cold at night and scorching heat during the long days. Electromagnetic storms whip silicon particles into abrasive clouds that can strip hull plating in hours.

Orbital surveys have identified ancient river channels and dried ocean basins, suggesting Kaldera Vast once held liquid water in vast quantities. Whatever cataclysm stripped the world of its hydrosphere left behind only dust and the ghost-geography of a drowned past.

The planet's enormous glass plains have attracted interest from materials engineers, while its relentless solar exposure makes it a candidate for large-scale energy harvesting. However, the punishing dust storms and extreme temperature differentials make any surface operation a logistical nightmare.
